statement.text:
a) We call a variety of groups a limit variety if it cannot be defined by finitely
many laws, while each of its proper subvarieties has a finite basis of identities. It
follows from Zorn’s lemma that every variety that has no finite basis of identities
contains a limit subvariety. Give explicitly (by means of identities or by a generating
group) at least one limit variety.                                    A. Yu. Olshanskii
